screens.title: Write it
screens.prose: Find the longest contiguous run of `nums` whose largest value minus its smallest is at most `limit`. Return its length. Return 0 for an empty list.
screens.question: Write `longest_within_limit(nums, limit)` in $O(n)$.

widget.starter:
from collections import deque

def longest_within_limit(nums, limit):
    # Keep a deque for the maximum and one for the minimum.
    return 1 if nums else 0
widget.how: Check runs 11 hidden tests: equal values, an empty list, one value, and the trap's list. Tests 8 to 11 have 100,000 values each, so a double loop over runs stops at test 8.

This version shrinks the window but never touches the deques:

```python
while left <= right and \
        nums[hi[0]] - nums[lo[0]] > limit:
    left += 1          # the deques are never touched
```

The input is `[4, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 2, 2]` with `limit = 0`.

explain.text: Stale fronts, first the 4 at index 0, then the 2 at index 1, keep the range at 2. Each window reads a range of 2 and shrinks to nothing, so the best stays 1. Dropping fronts below `left` fixes it, whether pops use `<=` or `<`.

screens.title: The pattern
screens.prose:
What you wrote, as a pattern:

```python
for right, x in enumerate(nums):
    pop hi while its back <= x; push right
    pop lo while its back >= x; push right
    while front(hi) - front(lo) > limit:
        left += 1; drop fronts below left
    best = max(best, right - left + 1)
```

screens.title: A calm stretch
screens.prose: A signal desk wants the longest stretch of ticks in which the price stayed within 5 pence of itself. Prices are in pence. Ticks arrive all day, so the method must be linear.
screens.question: Which structure answers it in one pass?

options.text: Two monotonic deques, one for the maximum and one for the minimum
One monotonic deque for the maximum
options.why: The maximum alone cannot tell you the range. You need the minimum too.

options.text: A heap of the window's prices
options.why: A heap gives one end cheaply, and removing an old price from it is slow.

options.why: That re-sorts at every step, far from linear.
